title: Flat as a pancake
caption: Edge-on spiral galaxy ESO 373-8, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: ESO 373-8 · constellation Antlia · about 25 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A thin, glittering streak crosses this Hubble image. It is the spiral galaxy ESO 373-8, seen edge-on some 25 million light-years away, with everything in it lined up in one flat plane. It belongs to the NGC 2997 group, along with at least seven neighbouring galaxies.

We see so many flat, pancake-like galaxies that their shape seems unremarkable. But why are galaxies flattened at all? The answer lies in a principle called conservation of angular momentum, which you can feel in a swivel chair: spin with arms and legs out, pull them in, and you speed up.

This galaxy started as a huge, slowly rotating ball of gas. As it collapsed under its own gravity its spin quickened until, like pizza dough flung and stretched in the air, it flattened into a disc. Anything that drifted up or down out of that disc was pulled back into line, leaving the neat, streamlined shape we see today.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.38 x 2.55 arcminutes) and distance (25 million light years), the frame spans roughly 25,000 × 19,000 light-years. Its light set out about 25 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines visible and near-infrared light captured by Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. The colour assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light included is invisible to the eye, and the long exposure collects far more light than an eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The same rule applies at every scale: angular momentum is conserved in a spinning galactic disc far across space just as it is for anyone twirling in an office chair.
alt: A thin, glittering edge-on galaxy stretched across the frame.
